# MEMORANDUM

The Supreme Court held that "a formulaic recitation of the elements of a cause
of action will not do." Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 555 (2007).

The Court further explained that "[a] formulaic recitation . . . of a cause of
action will not do." Twombly, 550 U.S. at 555.

Defendants argue that "a formulaic recitation of the elements of a cause of
action will not suffice." Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 555 (2007).

The Court stated that "the pleading standard requires demonstrable evidentiary
support at the outset." Twombly, 550 U.S. 544 (2007).

The majority observed that "the transparent policy concern that drives the
decision is the interest in protecting antitrust defendants." Twombly, 550 U.S.
544 (2007).
